claims.statement: GHES is distributed as a self-contained virtual appliance; after VM provisioning and appliance installation it runs Linux with a custom application stack. This describes packaging, not an installed healthy instance, supported arbitrary VM image, security assurance or permission to provision infrastructure.

The log-streaming sequence uses inspected enterprise-access, Settings and Audit log includes before selecting Log streaming. Enterprise access has a GHES versus other-context branch. Navigation does not prove configured streaming, delivery, retention, event completeness or safe sink credentials, and no stream was configured.

Within ghes-opentelemetry, OpenTelemetry is available from GHES 3.18 and described as enhancing observability, while collectd remains default and fully supported in the described release. Coexistence is not a completed migration, measured monitoring coverage or current collectd retirement.

The ghes-opentelemetry note identifies OpenTelemetry metrics as public preview and subject to change, with optional feedback to customer success or a community discussion. This historical preview is not current lifecycle verification, stable telemetry contract or authority to send external feedback; the discussion was not reviewed or contacted.

The GHES-only note says rate limits are disabled by default and recommends confirming instance limits with the site administrator. Default absence is not known actual configuration, exemption from every limit, capacity assurance or permission to increase traffic; no administrator was contacted or limits changed.

The fragment explicitly asks which roles can bypass the containing policy restrictions. Bypass is a security-relevant exception, not a generic allowlist of compliant actors; the policy, eligible roles, bypass mode and saved configuration are unspecified and no protection change was performed.
